title: Kamsa sees him everywhere
hookLine: in Kamsa's prison, a child is moved in secret, and a frightened king can't stop thinking about the next one
carry: smarana: keep the Lord in mind, always
tomorrow: what did the Lord look like the moment he was born?

cards: In the prison, Kamsa kills Devaki's children as they are born. The Bhagavata doesn't linger there. When six have died, the text says, a seventh child begins to grow in her.
And this time something is done in secret. The Lord, the Bhagavata says, calls on his own power of illusion, Yogamaya, and gives her a task. A child is in danger.

teach.b: Yogamaya draws the seventh child out of Devaki's womb and places him in the womb of Rohini, another wife of Vasudeva, living safely in Gokula, a village of cowherds across the river.
In the prison, people say Devaki has miscarried.

The Bhagavata names the child from that night: Sankarshana, the one who was drawn out. Later he is known as Balarama, Krishna's older brother, and the Lord himself calls him a part of Shesha, the serpent he rests on.
Then the Lord enters Vasudeva's mind, and from there passes into Devaki, and she begins to shine.
Kamsa sees her glowing and understands: this is the one. But he can't bring himself to kill a pregnant woman, so he waits, and the waiting turns into obsession.
Sitting, lying down, eating, walking, the text says, Kamsa saw that child everywhere. Later the Bhagavata draws a startling lesson from this.
Kamsa reached the Lord through fear, it says, others through hatred, the cowherd women through love.

teach.h: SMARANA: A MIND FIXED ON HIM
teach.b: What counts is a mind fixed on him.
Hindus call it smarana, remembering, and it's why a grandmother murmurs a name of God over the stove, in the car and in the checkout line: Kamsa's constant thought, chosen with love instead of fear.

teach.h: THE GODS SING TO THE UNBORN CHILD
teach.b: Meanwhile the gods come to the cell to sing to the child inside Devaki. Do not be afraid, mother, they tell her. The one you carry has come to protect the world.

how: The gods' prayer to the child in Devaki's womb is heard when the Bhagavata is recited, and Balarama is honored alongside Krishna in temples and festivals. Smarana, remembering God through the day, is lived in quiet repetition of a divine name, often on a mala of beads, and in greetings like 'Jai Shri Krishna'.

o: Krishna's coming, prepared in secret inside a prison
a festival the gods hold each year in heaven
the night Balarama is born to Devaki in the cell

games.q: before the birth — tap the pairs.
p: sees the child everywhere, from fear

s: Balarama is born to Devaki in the prison
he is moved to Rohini's womb in Gokula before he is born.
the gods come to the prison to praise the unborn child
Brahma, Shiva and the others sing, and tell Devaki not to fear.
Balarama is only Krishna's brother, nothing more
the Lord calls the child he moves a part of Shesha, the serpent he rests on.

games.q: you're Kamsa. your prisoner is glowing, and you're sure the child that will kill you is inside her. what do you do?
o: hold back, and wait for the birth.
games.why: he won't kill a pregnant woman, so he waits, and his fear makes him see the child in everything he does. the Bhagavata later counts even that as remembering the Lord.

practice: Pick one name of God you love, Krishna, Rama, Shiva, or simply Om, and say it softly under your breath while you do one ordinary task: rinsing a cup, walking to the door, waiting for a page to load.
Many Hindus do this all through the day. If you don't pray, choose one word that steadies you. Kamsa couldn't stop thinking of him out of fear; try a minute of it out of love.

wordCard.voice: The birth. Before it happens, a brother is moved to safety, a jailer can't stop thinking of the child, and the gods come to sing.

orig.note: sankarshana: the Bhagavata gives Balarama this name because he was drawn from one womb to another.

carryVoice: Smarana: keep the Lord in mind, always. That's your line. Tomorrow, midnight in the prison. See you then.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.2: the six children killed, Yogamaya and the transfer of the seventh child to Rohini, the name Sankarshana, the Lord entering Vasudeva and Devaki, Kamsa's fear, the prayer of the gods
Bhagavata Purana 10.2.8 (the Lord tells Yogamaya that his part called Shesha is in Devaki's womb)
Bhagavata Purana 7.1 (Narada: the gopis reached the Lord through desire, Kamsa through fear, Shishupala and others through hatred)
